questions.q: Two particles move at right angle to each other. Their de Broglie wavelengths are ${\lambda}_{1}$ and ${\lambda}_{2}$ respectively. The particles suffer perfectly inelastic collision. The de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of the final particle, is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{{P}_{1}} = \dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{1}}\overset{^}{i}\text{,}\overset{→}{{P}_{2}} = \dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{2}}\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{P} = \overset{→}{{P}_{1}} + \overset{→}{{P}_{2}} = \dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{1}}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{2}}\overset{^}{j}$
\left|\overset{→}{P}\right| = h\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}^{2}}}$
$\dfrac{h}{\lambda} = h\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}^{2}}}$
$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}^{2}}

questions.q: An oil drop of the radius $2$ mm with a density $3g{cm}^{- 3}$~is held stationary under a constant electric field $3 . 55 \times {10}^{5}Vm^{- 1}$ in the Millikan's oil drop experiment. What is the number of excess electrons that the oil drop will possess?  \left(\text{consider}g = 9 . 81ms^{- 2}\right)$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$qE = Mg⇒ neE = ρ\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right) \times g$
$⇒ n \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 3 . 55 \times {10}^{5}= 3 \times {10}^{3} \times \dfrac{4}{3} \times \pi \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)3 \times 9 . 81$
$⇒ n = 173 \times {10}^{( 3 - 9 - 5 + 19 )}⇒ n = 1 . 73 \times {10}^{10}$.

questions.q: The energy $E$ and momentum $p$ of a moving body of mass $m$ are related by some equation. Given that c represents the speed of light, identify the correct equation
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We need to check the dimensions only.
With momentum the dimension
$E^2=p^2 C^2$
And with mass $E^2=m^2 c^4$
So $E^2=p^2 C^2+m^2 c^4$ (dimensionally)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : The photoelectric effect does not take& place, if the energy of the incident radiation is less than the work function of a metal.

Reason R : Kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is zero, if the energy of the incident radiation is equal to the work function of a metal.
options: Both A& and R& are correct and R& is the correct explanation of A
Both A& and R& are correct but R& is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R& is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work function of a metal is defined as the minimum amount of energy needed for ejection of photoelectron. Therefore, Assertion is correct.

Incident energy may or may not be completely absorbed by the photoelectron. Therefore, kinetic energy of a& photoelectron may be zero even if the incident radiation has energy greater than work function. Hence, though the reason is correct, it is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.q:
The difference between threshold wavelengths for two metal surfaces $A$~and $B$ having work function~${ϕ}_{A} = 9eV$ and ${ϕ}_{B} = 4 . 5eV$ in $nm$~is:

{Given, hc = 1242eVnm}
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work function is given by&

$\dfrac{hc}{λ} = ϕ$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{hc}{ϕ}$

By the given data,

${λ}_{A} = \dfrac{1242}{9}nm$,~${λ}_{B} = \dfrac{1242}{4 . 5}nm$,~

The difference between the wavelengths,

${λ}_{B} - {λ}_{A} = \dfrac{1242}{4 . 5} - \dfrac{1242}{9}nm = \dfrac{1242}{9}nm$

$= 138nm$

questions.q: Consider two separate ideal gases of electrons and protons having same number of particles. The temperature of both the gases are same. The ratio of the uncertainty in determining the position of an electron to that of a proton is proportional to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$K . E . = \dfrac{3}{2}kT$
$⇒ \dfrac{p2}{2m} = \dfrac{3}{2}kT$
$⇒ p = \sqrt{3kTm}$
From Heisenberg uncertainty principle
$∴ \Deltax\Deltap = \dfrac{h}{4\pi}$
$\Deltax = \dfrac{h}{4\pi\Deltap} = \dfrac{h}{4\pi\sqrt{3kTm}}$
$∴ \Deltax ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$
$∴ \dfrac{\Delta{x}_{e}}{\Delta{x}_{p}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{mp}{me}}$

questions.q: When the wavelength of radiation falling on a metal is changed from& $500nmto200nm$, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons becomes three times larger. The work function of the metal is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${KE}_\max = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{500} - ϕ$~ ~.....(i)

Now,

$3{KE}_\max = \dfrac{hc}{200} - ϕ$

~ ~.....(ii)

From equation (i) and (ii)

\left(ii\right)\left(i\right) = \dfrac{3}{1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{hc}{200} - ϕ}{\dfrac{hc}{500} - ϕ}$

Put the value of~$hc = 1237 . 5$~and solving~$ϕ = 0 . 61eV$

$

questions.q: An electron of mass ' m ' with an initial velocity $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{v}_0 \hat{i}  \left(\mathrm{v}}_{0}\gt$0\right)$ enters an electric field $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{o}} \hat{\mathrm{k}}.$If the initial de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda_0$, the value after time t would be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{v}_0 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\frac{\mathrm{E}_0 \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}} t \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}|=\sqrt{\mathrm{v}_0^2+\frac{\mathrm{E}_0^2 \mathrm{e}^2 \mathrm{t}^2}{\mathrm{~m}^2}} \\ & \lambda_0=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}_0} \\ & \lambda^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}_0 \sqrt{1+\frac{\mathrm{E}_0^2 \mathrm{e}^2 \mathrm{t}^2}{\mathrm{v}_0^2 \mathrm{~m}^2}}} \\ & \lambda^{\prime}=\frac{\lambda_0}{\sqrt{1+\frac{\mathrm{E}_0^2 \mathrm{e}^2 \mathrm{t}^2}{\mathrm{v}_0^2 \mathrm{~m}^2}}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A small object at rest, absorbs a light pulse of power $20mW$ and duration $300$ ns. Assuming speed of light as $3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$. The momentum of the object becomes equal to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Momentum& $p = \dfrac{Energy\left(E\right)}{Speedoflight\left(c\right)}$

$= \dfrac{Power \times time}{c}$

$= \dfrac{\left(20 \times {10}^{- 3}W\right)\left(300 \times {10}^{- 9}s\right)}{3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}}$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 17}kgms^{- 1}$

As momentum is~conserved, therefore momentum of object will be~$2 \times {10}^{- 17}kgms^{- 1}$.

questions.q: A metal plate of area $1 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}$ is illuminated by a radiation of intensity $16\dfrac{milliW}{m2}$ . The work function of the metal is $5eV .$ The energy of the incident photons is $10$ eV and only $10%$ of it produces photo electrons.~The number of emitted photo electron~ per second and their maximum energy, respectively, will be:  \left[1eV = 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}J\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Einstein's photoelectric equation
Maximum $KE = \dfrac{hC}{\lambda} - ϕ$

$= 10 - 5$

$= 5eV$

Intensity $I = \dfrac{\left({N}_{p}\right)\dfrac{hC}{\lambda}}{tA} ⇒ \dfrac{{N}_{p}}{t} = \dfrac{IA}{\left(\dfrac{hC}{\lambda}\right)}$

and number of electrons per second. $= \left(\dfrac{{N}_{p}}{t}\right) \times 10%$

$= \left(\dfrac{IA}{\dfrac{hC}{\lambda}}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{16 \times {10}^{- 3} \times {10}^{- 4}}{10 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 10}$

$= {10}^{11}$ per sec

questions.q: An $\alpha$ particle and a proton are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. The ratio of linear momenta acquired by above two particals will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For $\alpha$~particle,~${m}_{α} = 4$~a.m.u and charge~${q}_{α} = 2e$.

For proton,~${m}_{p} = 1$~a.m.u and charge~${q}_{p} = e$.

As the charged particle are moving through same potential, the kinetic energy acquired by the particle will be equal to electric potential energy i.e.,~$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = qV$, where,~$V$~is potential.

Using the relation between momentum~ \left(p\right)$ and kinetic energy, we have~

$p = \sqrt{2mE} = \sqrt{2mqV}$

Then, the ratio of linear momenta of two particles is~$\dfrac{p\alpha}{pp} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{α}{q}_{α}}{{m}_{p}{q}_{p}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{1} \times \dfrac{2}{1}}$

$= \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{1} = 2\sqrt{2}: 1$

$

questions.q: The radiation pressure exerted by a 450 W light source on a perfectly reflecting surface placed at 2 m away from it, is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$P_{\mathrm{rad}}=\frac{2 I}{\mathrm{C}}$
Where $\mathrm{I}=$ intensity at surface
$\mathrm{C}=$ Speed of light
$\begin{aligned}
& I=\frac{\text { Power }}{\text { Area }}=\frac{450}{4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2} \\ & =\frac{450}{4 \pi \times 4}=\frac{450}{16 \pi} \\ & P_{\mathrm{rad}}=\frac{2 \times 450}{16 \pi \times 3 \times 10^8}=\frac{150}{8 \pi \times 10^8}
\end{aligned}$
$=5.97 \times 10^{-8} \approx 6 \times 10^{-8}$ Pascals

questions.q: An electron accelerated through a potential difference ${V}_{1}$~has a de-Broglie wavelength of $\lambda$. When the potential is changed to ${V}_{2}$, its de-Broglie wavelength increases by $50 %$. The value of~  \left(\dfrac{V1}{V2}\right)$& is equal to :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let initial wavelength be& $\lambda$, then after~$50 %$~increase wavelength will become~$1 . 5\lambda$.

Now,~$KE = \dfrac{P2}{2m} = eV \text{ and } P = \dfrac{h}{λ}$

Therefore,~$eV = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{h}{λ}\right)2}{2m}$.

So we can write

$e{V}_{1} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{h}{λ}\right)2}{2m} . . . Eq ( 1 )$~and~

$e{V}_{2} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{h}{1 . 5\lambda}\right)2}{2m} . . . Eq ( 2 )$

From both equations, we get

$\dfrac{V1}{V2} = \left(1 . 5\right)2 = \dfrac{9}{4}$

questions.q: When a metal surface is illuminated by light of wavelength $\lambda$, the stopping potential is $8V$. When the same surface is illuminated by light of wavelength $3\lambda$, stopping potential is $2V$. The threshold wavelength for this surface is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From photoelectric effect equation, we can write $E = ϕ + {K}_\max$

and work function can be written as $ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda0}$.

Also, maximum kinetic energy ${K}_\max = e{V}_{0}$

For first case:

$8e = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda0}$ ... (i)

For second case:

$2e = \dfrac{hc}{3\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda0}$ ... (ii)

After using equation (ii) in (i), we get

$4\left(\dfrac{hc}{3\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda0}\right) = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda0}$

$⇒ {λ}_{0} = 9\lambda$

$V = \dfrac{150}{7.5 \times 7.5 \times {10}^{- 4}} = \dfrac{80}{3}kV$

$V \approx 25KeV$ ~

questions.q:
A metal exposed to light of wavelength $800$ nm and emits photoelectrons with a certain kinetic energy. The maximum kinetic energy of photo-electron doubles when light of wavelength $500$ nm is used. The work function of the metal is

(Take $hc = 1230eV - nm$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation

${k}_\max = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ$

$⇒ {k}_{1} = \dfrac{1230}{800} - ϕ . . . \left(1\right)$

And~$⇒ {k}_{2} = $\dfrac{1230}{500} -$ϕ$

Since,~${k}_{2} = 2{k}_{1}$

$⇒ 2{k}_{1} = $\dfrac{1230}{500} -$ϕ . . . \left(2\right)$

Eliminating ${k}_{1}$ from (1) and (2) we get

$0 = \dfrac{1230}{500} - \dfrac{1230}{400} +ϕ$

$⇒ ϕ = 0 . 615eV$

questions.q: When light of frequency twice the threshold frequency is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of emitted electron is ${v}_{1}$. When the frequency of incident radiation is increased to five times the threshold value, the maximum velocity of emitted electron becomes ${v}_{2}$. If ${v}_{2} = x{v}_{1}$, the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum kinetic energy is expressed as& ${K}_\max = hf - ϕ$, here,~$ϕ$~is~work function of metal.

For first case,~$\dfrac{1}{2}{m{v}_{1}}^{2} = h \left[ \left($2{f}_{0}\right) - {f}_{0}\right]$

For second case,~\dfrac{1}{2}{m{v}_{2}}^{2} =$h \left[ \left(5{f}_{0}\right) - {f}_{0}\right]$

$⇒ $\dfrac{{v}_{2}2}{{v}_{1}2} = \dfrac{4}{1}$⇒ $\dfrac{v2}{v1} =$2$

$

questions.q: A point source of light is placed at the centre of curvature of a hemispherical surface. The source emits a power of $24W$.~The radius of curvature of hemisphere is $10$ cm and the inner surface is completely reflecting. The force on the hemisphere due to the light falling on it is ______~$\times {10}^{- 8}N$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For completely reflecting surface, force,& $F = \dfrac{2IA}{c}$, where,~$I = \dfrac{P}{Surfacearea}$~is intensity of radiation,~$A$~is surface area and~$c$~is speed of light.

$F = \dfrac{2I}{c}\piR^{2} = 2\dfrac{P0}{4\piR^{2}}\dfrac{\piR^{2}}{c}$

$= \dfrac{P0}{2c} = \dfrac{24}{2 \times 3 \times {10}^{8}} = 4 \times {10}^{- 8}N$

questions.q:
The surface of a metal is illuminated alternately with photons of energies ${E}_{1} = 4eV$~and~${E}_{2} = 2 . 5eV$~respectively.~The ratio of maximum speeds of the photoelectrons emitted in the two cases is $2 .$ The work function of the metal in $( eV )$ is..........
&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Energy of two photons& are& ${E}_{1} = 4eV$~and~${E}_{2} = 2 . 5eV$

The ratio of maximum speeds of the photoelectrons emitted in the two cases is $\dfrac{v1}{v2} = 2$

Using Einstein equation of photoelectric effect,

$K{E}_\max = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = E - ϕ . . . ( 1 )$

Where,~$ϕ$~is the work function of metal and~$E$~is the energy of photon

Now using equation for both the cases we get,

~$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = 4 - ϕ \ldots ( 2 )$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} = 2 . 5 - ϕ . . . ( 3 )$

Dividing equation (2) and (3)~and substitute given values, we get,

$\dfrac{{v}_{1}2}{{v}_{2}2} = \dfrac{4 - ϕ}{2 . 5 - ϕ} = \left(2\right)2$

$⇒ 3ϕ = 6$

$⇒ ϕ = 2eV$
